articles.content: Abstract: The remarkable generation quality of modern diffusion models often comes at the cost of massive parameter counts, which necessitate server-side inference with significant computational costs and potential privacy risks. Consequently, there is growing momentum toward developing efficient on-device alternatives. While recent efforts have optimized text-to-image models for mobile hardware, they remain relatively bulky, typically ranging from 0.5B to 1B parameters. We present BlazeEdit, a highly efficient, generalist image-to-image diffusion model tailored for on-device deployment. articles.content: We Audited the Same Codebase with Claude Opus 4.8 and MiniMax M3 Kilo Blog Subscribe Sign in We Audited the Same Codebase with Claude Opus 4.8 and MiniMax M3 Darko Gjorgjievski Jun 05, 2026 9 2 1 Share Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.8 on May 28, 2026 , and MiniMax shipped MiniMax M3 on June 1, 2026. The two models sit at very different price points, and we wanted to see how they perform compared to each other. We gave the same code audit task to Claude Opus 4.8 at four reasoning levels and to MiniMax M3, then tracked tokens, cost, time, and how many known issues each run found. TL;DR: MiniMax M3 surfaced 13 of 17 known issues for about $0.07, the same count as Claude Opus 4.8 at medium and high and two behind Claude Opus 4.8 at xhigh and max. Claude Opus 4.8 caught the most issues at its

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Cost per issue found is the cleanest view. MiniMax M3 won by a wide margin. Claude at max was the most expensive per finding. The two settings that found the most were not the most efficient per dollar.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: But more reasoning did not move in one direction. Claude at medium and high both caught an async-transaction bug that xhigh and max missed. And Claude at max cost $3.39, which is 67% more than xhigh, on slightly fewer tokens, for nothing better.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: MiniMax M3 held up on the specific code-path bugs too. The endpoint returning a stored secret. A list filter that dropped a condition. The replay path accepting deliveries in the wrong state. It landed at 13 of 17. Claude at xhigh and max led the field at 15.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: What each run caught is where it gets interesting. Every run flagged the big blockers: missing auth on every route, unsafe outbound requests, a non-constant-time signature check, a worker that could send the same webhook twice, missing idempotency.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Going in, the price gap is steep. Claude Opus 4.8 runs about 8x higher on input tokens and 10x higher on output.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: The fixture: a webhook delivery service in TypeScript, Bun, and SQLite, with 17 real bugs we catalogued ourselves first. That list was the answer key. Same prompt every run: audit it for security, reliability, correctness, and coverage, write the report, don't touch the code. We ran Claude at four reasoning levels and MiniMax M3 at its default.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
